learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will become a master Grammar Detective, easily spotting hidden mistakes in sentences and polishing them into perfect Hindi!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Just like a machine needs all its gears aligned to work, a sentence needs its words aligned! Mistakes happen when we mess up the word order (Padkram), use the wrong gender or number (Anvay), or use unnecessary extra words. Fixing these is called Vakya Shuddhikaaran.

Hindi follows a strict 'Subject -> Object -> Verb' rule. Placing words in the wrong spot creates hilarious but incorrect sentences! 
Wrong: 'गाय का ताकतवर दूध होता है' (Cow's strong milk is there). 
Right: 'गाय का दूध ताकतवर होता है' (Cow's milk is strong).

The Verb MUST always match the Subject in Gender (Ling) and Number (Vachan). If the subject is feminine, the verb must be feminine! 
Wrong: 'मीरा गाना गा रहा है' (Meera is singing - 'raha' is masculine). 
Right: 'मीरा गाना गा रही है' ('rahi' correctly matches Meera).

This happens when we use two words that mean the exact same thing in one sentence. It is totally unnecessary! 
Wrong: 'वह वापस लौट आया' (He returned back - 'wapas' and 'laut' mean the same). 
Right: 'वह लौट आया' (He returned).

Using the wrong case marker (Karak Chihn) changes or destroys the meaning. 
Wrong: 'मेरे को बाजार जाना है' (A very common slang error!). 
Right: 'मुझे बाजार जाना है' (I have to go to the market).

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♀️ The Grammar Doctor Clinic
fun_activity.instructions:
These 3 sentences are 'sick' with grammar errors. Be the doctor and write out their cured, correct forms! 
1. 'मेरे को एक सेब खाना है।' 
2. 'हवा ठंडा चल रहा है।' 
3. 'केवल मात्र दो रुपये दे दो।'

quick_recap: ⭐ Vakya Shuddhikaaran is the process of finding and fixing grammatical errors in a sentence.
⭐ Padkram (Word Order) errors happen when words are placed in the wrong position.
⭐ Anvay errors happen when the Verb doesn't match the Gender or Number of the Subject.
⭐ Karak errors involve using incorrect joining words (like 'mere ko' instead of 'mujhe').
⭐ Avoid Punrukti (repetition) by never using two words with the exact same meaning together.
